paragraphs: Friend, here's what this chapter shows me. Judah said one thing to Tamar and did another. He told her to wait for Shelah, and then he let Shelah grow up and never sent for her (Genesis 38:11, 14). Broken promises don't disappear just because nobody mentions them. They sit there like dough left out overnight, and sooner or later somebody has to deal with them.

Then the day comes when Judah is the one who gets caught. Tamar sends his own seal and cord and staff back to him and asks, "Whose seal and cord and staff are these?" (Genesis 38:25). And Judah doesn't argue, doesn't dodge and doesn't blame anybody. He says, "She is more righteous than I…" (Genesis 38:26). Friend, that is hard to say out loud. I think it might be the biggest moment in the whole chapter.

Now look at where this family ends up. Perez and Zerah are born, and the Gospel of Matthew names them both in the line of Jesus Christ (Matthew 1:1, 3). This is a messy chapter with messy people, and God still keeps His plan moving through them. So if you've got a mess in your own story, don't hide it. Own it, bring it to Him and keep baking, because He doesn't need a spotless kitchen to do something wonderful.
